mechanism_narrative: Sustained positive GROCERY_PHARM mobility (+13.4 to +15.4 over three weeks) indicates consistent essential-trip behavior. This baseline activity anchors consumer confidence and foot traffic patterns, driving retail-recreation mobility upward over the next four weeks as consumers gain confidence to make discretionary trips alongside essential ones.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM remained positive and stable across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase relative to the last 28 days, or GROCERY_PHARM falls below +10 percent change in any of the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Negative PARKS mobility (-11.7 to -13.9 over three weeks) combined with stable negative RETAIL_REC (-15.0 to -16.0) indicates suppressed discretionary outdoor activity. When PARKS mobility reverses to positive, consumers redirect substituted leisure demand toward indoor retail-recreation venues, producing a directional increase in RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses from negative to positive week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS has been consistently negative across all four weeks
failure_condition: PARKS mobility remains negative or flat in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase when PARKS turns positive.

mechanism_narrative: Rising TRANSIT mobility (6.4 to 8.7 over three weeks) signals increasing commuter and public-space traffic. This upward trend in transit use creates spillover foot traffic to retail-recreation venues located near transit hubs, amplifying RETAIL_REC gains over the next four weeks through proximity-driven consumer exposure.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT increases by more than 1.5 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from 6.4 to 8.7 over three weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility plateaus or declines in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC fails to increase despite sustained TRANSIT gains.

mechanism_narrative: Interaction between rising WORKPLACES mobility (−3.4 to +2.0 over three weeks) and stable TRANSIT gains (6.4 to 8.7) indicates return of commuting routines. Workers traveling to offices pass through retail-recreation zones; combined effect of workplace return and transit availability drives RETAIL_REC upward within two weeks as commute-adjacent shopping resumes.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above zero and TRANSIT remains above 7.0 simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES crossed zero in week t-2w and remained positive
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES falls below zero or TRANSIT drops below 7.0 in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase despite both conditions being met.

mechanism_narrative: Declining RESIDENTIAL mobility (8.6 to 5.1 over three weeks) indicates consumers spending less time at home. This outbound mobility shift, combined with stable GROCERY_PHARM (+13-15), suggests consumers are substituting home time for out-of-home activity. RETAIL_REC will increase as RESIDENTIAL continues to decline, capturing displaced home-time activity.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 8.6 to 5.1 over three weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility stabilizes or increases above 5.0 in the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase despite RESIDENTIAL continuing to decline.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent negative RETAIL_REC (−15 to −16 over four weeks) in a regime of rising TRANSIT and positive GROCERY_PHARM indicates policy-driven retail restrictions remain in place despite partial reopening of transit and essential services. RETAIL_REC will remain negative or decline further over the next four weeks if restrictions persist, as the gap between essential and discretionary mobility widens.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC remains below −14 while TRANSIT and GROCERY_PHARM remain positive
evidence_refs: fact:Retail-recreation remains suppressed despite essential-service mobility gains
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases above −12 in the next four weeks, or policy restrictions on retail are explicitly lifted.

mechanism_narrative: Stable negative PARKS mobility (−11.7 to −13.9) over four weeks indicates seasonal or weather-driven suppression of outdoor activity. As seasonal conditions improve or weather shifts, PARKS mobility will reverse, and consumers will reallocate discretionary time from indoor retail-recreation back to outdoor venues, causing RETAIL_REC to decline within one week of PARKS reversal.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility increases by more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS has been consistently negative and stable across four weeks
failure_condition: PARKS mobility does not increase in the next week, or RETAIL_REC does not decline when PARKS reverses sharply positive.

RETAIL_REC will increase over the next four weeks as the only available discretionary destination for outbound mobility, unless PARKS reverses or new restrictions emerge.

evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declining while PARKS remains suppressed
